html:
The capital of Cuba and for centuries the key port of the Spanish Caribbean. Founded in 1514 on another site, it moved to its present harbour around 1519.

Its deep, sheltered harbour lay where the Gulf Stream carries ships out of the Gulf of Mexico toward Europe. From the 1560s the Spanish treasure fleets gathered there each year, loaded with silver from Mexico and Peru, before sailing together to Spain. To guard them, Spain built strong forts such as El Morro, and later walled the city. Pirates and rival powers raided it. Britain captured it in 1762, during the Seven Years' War, and handed it back a year later in exchange for Florida.

In the 1800s Havana grew rich on sugar worked by enslaved Africans, and on tobacco and cigars. It was the stage of Cuba's wars of independence and, in 1959, of the Cuban Revolution. Its old town is a World Heritage Site.
